storyboard.claim: The Golds claim the right to whip Reds because they survived the Institute.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A Gold guard in black armour points down at a Red, the threat made physical.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the chunk on the Gold creed quoted in the narration.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pointing guard turns the quoted boast into a threat aimed at the viewer's Red.

storyboard.claim: Their own suffering justifies inflicting more suffering on others.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A proud Gold student smirks and points outward, the cruelty being justified.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the creed: the Golds' pain as excuse.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk gives the justification an edge of cruelty rather than sympathy.

storyboard.claim: The narrative they tell themselves is a cage, but one that lets them rule.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains for the cage of the myth, with a Gold student thinking about his own story.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The creed from 241 is now named as a cage.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chains icon gives the cage a literal bound-by reading; the thinking pose suggests the story is held in the mind.

storyboard.claim: The Golds must believe the Institute is a pure meritocracy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A Gold student thinking hard, the belief being worked on.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the myth the cage from 242 holds in place.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout names the myth in the narrator's words; the thinking pose shows effort to believe it.

storyboard.claim: A myth system has rot at the foundation, which leads to corruption at the top.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow from the myth, through rot, to corruption.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the Gold creed to the structure beneath it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The flow shows the cause-to-effect chain the narration sets out.

storyboard.claim: The meritocracy is rigged by the powerful.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer icon: one hand controlling the result behind a proud Gold student.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the corruption from 244 as rigging.
storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer icon reads as one person controlling others, which is the rigging.

storyboard.claim: The Institute's students are thrown into a massive wilderness war game.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A war icon over a wide snowy horizon with Darrow walking into the field.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Darrow's Institute path begins here.
storyboard.addedInformation: The war icon gives the game a literal military reading.

callout.text: FIGHTING IN THE MUD AND SNOW

storyboard.claim: Students conquer castles and enslave each other in the mud and snow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow and Titus fighting in the snow, impact bursts between them.
storyboard.onScreenText: FIGHTING IN THE MUD AND SNOW
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the game from 246 as violence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two cast members make the fight readable as a fight, not a single angry man.

storyboard.claim: The adult proctors live in floating fortresses, acting like gods over the game.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A Gold guard high in the sky, looking down and pointing from above.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the game to the rulers who oversee it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The high sky set and low angle make the gods-above-the-children reading literal.

storyboard.claim: Darrow becomes a warlord leading an army in winter and sees the proctors interfering.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A war icon over a winter horizon with Darrow pointing his bow ahead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Darrow rises from player to leader.
storyboard.addedInformation: The war icon marks him as a commander, not just a student.

storyboard.claim: Darrow fires an arrow at Proctor Apollo in the snow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target icon as Darrow aims a bow at a distant adult Gold.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Darrow acts on his interference suspicion from 249.
storyboard.addedInformation: The target icon reads as aiming, which is the arrow shot.

storyboard.claim: The arrow pings off an invisible pulse shield and Apollo does not flinch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon over a Gold guard standing unmoved in the snow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The arrow from 250 hits the shield.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield icon shows protection; the blank face shows he is unbothered.

callout.text: SNOW MELTS BEFORE IT TOUCHES HIM

storyboard.claim: Apollo's energy melts snow before it touches him, while starving Reds freeze.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A Gold guard in the snowfield, flakes dissolving before his body.
storyboard.onScreenText: SNOW MELTS BEFORE IT TOUCHES HIM
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the shield into the untouchable image.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout makes the melting-snow image readable as the protection.

storyboard.claim: The students are subjected to harsh nature to prove their worth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy icon over Darrow slumped in the snow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the melting-snow image into the purpose of the trial.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trophy icon marks worth as rank, the prize the trial is for.

storyboard.claim: The rulemakers are insulated from the hardship, and the viewer is addressed directly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator points outward at the viewer, the pivot to you.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A pivot from the trial to the rulers.
storyboard.addedInformation: The point turns the commentary toward the viewer.

callout.text: TOOLS TO KEEP YOU IN PLACE

storyboard.claim: The rules are tools to keep the lower in place, and the rule-makers do not play by them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow confronts a Gold guard, pointing at him.
storyboard.onScreenText: TOOLS TO KEEP YOU IN PLACE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the insulation in 254 matters.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two-shot shows the confrontation the narration describes.

storyboard.claim: Apollo and other proctors sabotage Darrow and drop supplies to a rival.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gift icon as Darrow thinks about the supplies given to the rival.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Apollo's confrontation from 255 uncovers the sabotage.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gift icon reads as something given away, the supplies to the rival.

storyboard.claim: Augustus threatened, bribed and blackmailed the proctors to rig the Institute.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer icon over a Gold guard casually pointing, the admission.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Apollo's reply from 256: he does not deny it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer icon reads as one ruler controlling the game.

storyboard.claim: The Institute is the Golds' sacred proving ground, the holy thing they believe in.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy icon with Darrow surprised, reacting to the holy proving ground.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Darrow reacts to the rigging from 257.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trophy icon marks the Institute as the prize of merit.

storyboard.claim: The ultimate test of merit is bought and sold by a politician for his son.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A smirking Gold guard in the arena, the sale implied by the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The sacred ground from 258 is sold.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout carries the buying-and-selling of merit in the narrator's words.

storyboard.claim: The rules are tools to keep the lower tiers in place.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julian slumped in a room, the lower tiers pinned down.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The sold merit from 259 reveals the lower tiers held down.
storyboard.addedInformation: The kind Gold's sad slump shows the cost to those below.

storyboard.claim: The elites at the very top see the rules as tools.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A smirking Gold student pointing up, the elites above.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrator pivots to who uses the rules.
storyboard.addedInformation: The upward point marks the top of the hierarchy.

storyboard.claim: Apollo is practically a god to these kids, with a pulse shield, grav boots and weapons.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow looks up with fear and points at a Gold figure in the sky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Apollo's power is introduced before the question.
storyboard.addedInformation: The afraid face shows the awe a child feels for the god-like figure.

storyboard.claim: Why is the cheating treated as a fragile secret when Apollo could just kill Darrow?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A Gold guard points angrily at Darrow in the arena, the threat behind the secret.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The god from 262 is shown holding the secret.
storyboard.addedInformation: The angry pointing makes the threat literal rather than an abstract puzzle.

storyboard.claim: If the secret gets out, the entire society burns, and the powerful golds would see it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A Gold guard warns Darrow with an angry point in the arena.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question of 263.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout names the stake in the narrator's words.

storyboard.claim: Exposing Augustus's rigging would break the illusion and trigger civil war.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow afraid and thinking, the illusion breaking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The stake from 264 gets its mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: The afraid face shows the fear of civil war.

storyboard.claim: The gold hierarchy is apex golds ruling lesser golds, and golds ruling reds.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-bucket sorter: apex golds, lesser golds, reds.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the hierarchy behind the revolt in 265.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sorter shows the three layers the narration names.

storyboard.claim: Lesser golds accept subservience only because they believe in the meritocracy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julian sad and thinking, the belief he is forced to hold.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hierarchy from 266 is accepted through belief.
storyboard.addedInformation: The kind Gold's sad face makes the acceptance feel costly.

callout.text: BORN LUCKY TO A RICH FATHER

storyboard.claim: The Jackal wins because he was born lucky to a rich father who can bribe the referees.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julian worried and thinking, realizing the win is inherited luck.
storyboard.onScreenText: BORN LUCKY TO A RICH FATHER
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The belief from 267 is undone by the realization.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout states the luck in the narrator's words.

storyboard.claim: If the game is rigged the myth collapses and the lesser golds will revolt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julian afraid, the myth collapsing as the callout lands.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The realization from 268 leads to revolt.
storyboard.addedInformation: The afraid face shows fear of the revolt.

storyboard.claim: The apex rulers need the illusion of pure merit to keep their own class from tearing them apart.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus smirking and talking, the illusion held up.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the myth from 269 matters to the top.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk shows the rulers managing the illusion on purpose.

storyboard.claim: The narrative is the only thing keeping the golds from fighting each other, and the hypocrisy is structural.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus and a Gold guard fighting, impact bursts between them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The illusion from 270 would give way to this fight.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two cast members make the infighting readable as a fight.

storyboard.claim: Darrow is a Red from the deep mines disguised as a Gold, exposing their hypocrisy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A mask icon with Darrow thinking, hidden behind a false face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fight from 271 is the danger; this is Darrow's disguise.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask reads as a false public face, which is his disguise.

storyboard.claim: Pure vengeance is a danger, not a plan to tear the castle down.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow angry and pointing, the vengeance he is tempted by.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Darrow's mask from 272 leads to his temptation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The angry point shows the rage the callout names.

storyboard.claim: Breaking the narrative with violence does not dismantle the cage; it replicates it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains icon with Titus angry and pointing, the rage that reproduces the cage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The danger from 273 is embodied in Titus.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chains icon reads as bound, the cage the violence keeps rebuilding.

storyboard.claim: Titus is a massive, brutal warlord of House Series.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus, tall and broad in his gilded uniform, angry and pointing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the figure of 274.
storyboard.addedInformation: The angry face and gilded uniform show the threat.

storyboard.claim: Titus plays the game with sheer terror rather than strategy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus angry and talking, the terror he spreads.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes Titus from 275 as a force of terror.
storyboard.addedInformation: The angry face conveys the menace the callout names.

storyboard.claim: Darrow confronts Titus in the dark halls of a captured castle, woozy and dragging himself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow worried and walking in a dark hall, Titus beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Titus from 276 meets Darrow in the castle.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dark hall and worried face show Darrow's weakened state.

storyboard.claim: Titus, yelling in rage, slips and uses the word bloody dam.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus angry, pointing down at Darrow in the castle hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The confrontation from 277 gets the slip.
storyboard.addedInformation: The angry point over Darrow shows the yelling.

storyboard.claim: Titus calls Darrow's curved weapon a sling blade, a word no Gold should know.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow surprised, the sling blade word landing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The slip from 278 reveals the red word.
storyboard.addedInformation: The surprised face shows Darrow realizing the slip matters.
